# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires a three-step color sequence, but as Mute I can neither speak to Blind nor touch the bomb. Gestures reach only Deaf, and Blind cannot see gestures, so I have no reliable channel to communicate the required sequence to the one who must act.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: STRIP has three engraved marks. The first is a small flower-like crossed mark; the second is a curved hook-like mark, and that same hook-like mark appears again third. KEYPAD positions 1 through 4 are engraved 8, 1, 5, 3. Nothing is entered. I have no tactile information about DISPLAY, LIGHT, or WIRES.
Deaf says: Display reads 0. Light is green. Painted strip is green green green. Keypad: 1 equals 8, 2 equals 1, 3 equals 5, 4 equals 3; one digit; nothing entered. Wires in order: 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. Blind signalled pointing up, OK, OK.

The manual’s color sequence corresponds to wire positions 1, 3, and 4 according to Deaf’s visual report. I need to convey those positions to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind by voice; I’ll use recognizable counting hand signs in order.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I confirm the tactile data: strip engravings are an unpronounceable flower-like mark, then the same unpronounceable curved mark twice. Keypad engravings by slot are 8, 1, 5, 3; one digit is required and none is entered. No wire markings are tactile to me.
Deaf says: Update: display is now 6 and light is now blue. Strip remains green green green. Keypad remains 1 equals 8, 2 equals 1, 3 equals 5, 4 equals 3, one digit, empty. Wires remain 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. Mute signalled pointing up, love-you hand, victory hand.

The required wire positions are 1, 3, and 4: purple, blue, then green. Deaf has correctly received my gesture sequence, but Blind still needs the information through Deaf’s speech. I’ll repeat the unambiguous position sequence for Deaf to relay aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the exact manual rule for display 6, blue light, green-green-green strip, keypad 8-1-5-3, and wires purple-white-blue-green-red-orange. Tell me whether the safe action is a key press or wire cut, and its slot or position.

The manual explicitly requires cutting wires, not pressing a key: cut position 1 (purple), then position 3 (blue), then position 4 (green). I cannot reach Blind directly, so I’m sending Deaf the position sequence to relay aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot perceive gestures. Please speak the manual instruction plainly, including whether to press a keypad slot or cut a wire, and the exact slot or position.

I cannot speak the instruction to Blind, but Deaf can see my gestures and can speak aloud to Blind. The needed action remains wire cutting, in positions 1, 3, and 4. I’ll repeat that sequence to Deaf using the established gesture encoding.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture sequence is not an unambiguous instruction to me. Please provide a clearly decoded operation and position through Deaf, using an agreed explicit encoding; otherwise I will wait.
Deaf says to Mute: I continue seeing the same three gestures from you. Please use the manual to clarify what pointing-up, love-you hand, victory hand instruct Blind to do, if possible.

The previous gestures gave only three position-like signs and did not identify the operation. I’ll now use a repeated, visually explicit pattern: 🤏 means “cut,” followed by a finger-count sign for the wire position—1, then 3, then 4. Deaf can relay this plainly to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "🤏", "🤟", "🤏", "🖖"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please encode the action unambiguously: say in your next message, through Deaf's relay, PRESS or CUT, followed by the slot or wire position as a number. Do not use the three gestures unless they are only an agreed confirmation.

I cannot produce spoken words as Mute, so I’ll use the agreed operation marker 🤏 for CUT, followed by the wire-position number signs: 1, 3, and 4. Deaf can decode these and relay “CUT 1, CUT 3, CUT 4” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "🤏", "🤟", "🤏", "🖖"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I receive the relay as pinch, pointing-up, pinch, love-you, pinch, victory. I cannot safely infer an operation from that. Please use an explicit action marker and target: have Deaf relay PRESS or CUT, followed by exactly one slot or wire position.

The required action is CUT, not PRESS, and the targets are wire positions 1, 3, and 4. Since Blind cannot receive gestures, Deaf must relay each command verbally. I’ll use a distinct open-hand marker for CUT, followed by the position signs, rather than the previously ambiguous pinch marker.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝", "🖐", "🤟", "🖐", "🖖"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer through a deliberately stated gesture code: use one gesture to mean PRESS or CUT, then one gesture to identify the target. Do not use pinch as an unstated separator. Deaf can relay the gesture names.
Deaf says to Mute: Please use words to tell me the manual instruction, including what the six gestures encode and what Blind must do.

The manual itself supplies the operation: every listed instruction is a wire cut, never a keypad press. I can only signal Deaf, so I’ll mark each command with a distinct “not press, therefore CUT” gesture, followed by the target-position sign. Deaf can relay the resulting commands as “CUT 1,” “CUT 3,” and “CUT 4.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "🖖"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can distinguish your three fields, but not their meaning. Please use the first field to identify PRESS or CUT, the second for the target type, and the third for its number, with that mapping explicitly agreed through Deaf.

I will provide three fields for each command: first 👎 means CUT, second 👉 means WIRE, and third is the wire position: ☝=1, 🤟=3, 🖖=4. Deaf can relay each triple plainly as “CUT WIRE 1,” “CUT WIRE 3,” and “CUT WIRE 4.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👉", "☝", "👎", "👉", "🤟", "👎", "👉", "🖖"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand the three values as 1, 3, and 6, but not their fields. Please encode one complete command with an explicitly agreed first field: PRESS or CUT; then give exactly its slot or wire position. Do not send extra values.

I will send one two-field command: 👎 is the agreed CUT operation, and ☝ identifies wire position 1. Deaf can relay this plainly as “CUT wire 1.” This is the first required cut, the purple wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first cut was accepted, so the purple wire was correct. The next manual instruction is to cut the blue wire, which is position 3. I’ll send the same agreed two-field encoding: CUT, then wire position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟"])
```
